item.title: NDC opens new Abuja base, targets 2027 electoral victory
item.description: …As Dickson hails new national secretariat as Noah’s Ark 2 By Henry Umoru The National Leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, has inaugurated its newly acquired national secretariat in Abuja as part of efforts to strengthen its operations ahead of the 2027 general election. The facility, located in the Jabi area of the Federal Capital Territory, was unveiled shortly after an emergency meeting of the party’s National Executive Committee (NEC), as it marks a significant step in the party’s efforts to strengthen its organisational structure and establish a permanent administrative base as preparations for the forthcoming elections gather momentum. The new secretariat is expected to serve as the party’s administrative centre and headquarters for its presidential campaign as preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum, just as the development marks a step in the NDC’s efforts to establish a permanent national base for coordinating its activities and managing its expanding political structure. It is a strategic centre for coordinating its activities, strengthening communication among state chapters and mobilising supporters across the country and is also expected to play a central role in organising the party’s presidential campaign and coordinating other electoral activities ahead of the 2027 general elections In his remarks, the National Leader of the party, Senator Seriake Dickson, described the facility as its new “Noah’s Ark” ahead of the 2027 general elections as he congratulated members and supporters on the acquisition, describing the new secretariat as a unifying centre that would provide a befitting home for the party’s growing membership. He referred to the facility as the NDC’s newly acquired “Noah’s Ark,” a description underscoring its importance as a rallying point for members and supporters as the party pursues its political ambitions. The inauguration attracted the party’s National Chairman, Senator Moses Cleopas; National Leader, Senator Seriake Dickson; and Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central in the National Assembly. Also present was the party’s Rivers State governorship candidate, Dumo Lulu-Briggs, alongside other party leaders and members. With this, the NDC has positioned itself as an alternative political platform for Nigerians seeking a change from the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). With the new facility, the party is expected to strengthen coordination between its national leadership, state chapters and other structures as election preparations continue. item.title: OPHK troops destroy ISWAP enclaves in Lake Chad, kill 16 terrorists
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Hadin Kai have neutralised 16 suspected Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters during coordinated air and artillery strikes on three suspected terrorist locations in the Tunbunma area of South Lake Chad, following intelligence on the presence of key terrorist leaders and fighters. According to the Joint Task Force, the operation followed sustained and relentless offensive against terrorist networks in the Lake Chad Basin. “The operation was conducted between 1 am and 2 am on 26 October 2026, using air and ground weapon systems to engage the identified locations. “Battle Damage Assessment indicates that 16 ISWAP fighters were neutralised across the targeted locations. “Among those reportedly killed were Abu Zubiru, an Arab national, and two associates, Baana Nglewa and Jindullah Sadiq, alongside other fighters. “Additionally, Abu Saleem, identified as the Wali of Tunbunma, sustained severe injuries alongside seven others. “Operation Hadin Kai reaffirms that there is no hiding place for terrorists and remains committed to restoring peace and normalcy while conducting intelligence-led operations against terrorist elements in the North East. “Members of the public are encouraged to provide timely and credible information to security agencies to support ongoing counter-terrorism operations.” The post OPHK troops destroy ISWAP enclaves in Lake Chad, kill 16 terrorists appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Microsoft offers voluntary exit packages to 60,000 staff
item.description: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, the company said on Monday, roughly a quarter of its workforce, as the tech giant seeks to cut costs while pouring money into artificial intelligence. Staff on select teams in the United States, Canada, India and Britain at vice president level and below will be eligible, a Microsoft spokesperson said, while some groups of employees, including some working on data centers, sales and marketing, are excluded. “The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we’re evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter,” Amy Coleman, an executive vice president and chief people officer, told employees in a memo. It’s the second voluntary buyout offer that Microsoft has offered employees this year. In April, the company reportedly offered around seven percent of its US workforce the option to retire early. Around 30 percent of those eligible took the voluntary retirement plan, according to CNBC. Microsoft had 223,000 employees globally at the end of June, down from 228,000 at the end of 2025, according to regulatory filings. Around 27 percent of Microsoft’s workforce is eligible for the new buyout offer. The company is expected to report quarterly earnings later this week. item.title: Niger APC raises 525-member campaign council, targets 2m votes for Tinubu/Bago
item.description: By Clare Nnabuike Niger State Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago has declared that his party, the All Progressives Congress (APC), is targeting 2 million votes to defeat the opposition parties in the 2027 presidential and governorship elections. The governor made this known on Monday at the inauguration of a 525-member State Presidential/Gubernatorial Campaign Council of the APC in Minna, where he revealed that the council is drawn from commissioners, special advisers, local government chairmen, councillors, state and national lawmakers, ministers, directors-general and coordinators. Bago described the structure as spanning party units to the state level and including political appointees, with total membership exceeding 100,000 over the years. “If everybody would bring its own votes, it would give us more than 1 million votes. But our target is beyond that. The ambition this time around is to bring out over 2 million votes, and by the grace of God we will do that,” he said. The governor urged the party to welcome returnees who had earlier defected to other parties, crediting the APC’s emergence as a coalition of parties that defeated the main opposition. He called for constructive media coverage and warned against overheating the polity or triggering insecurity, saying the campaign would highlight the federal government’s economic policies, improved revenue and job creation. Bago cited recent infrastructure and security gains, including better roads and freer movement of goods in parts of the state, as part of what the government has done and disclosed that the North Central Presidential Campaign office in Minna would be commissioned next week, with possible attendance of the President, Vice President, Senate President, Speaker or National Chairman. Minister of Information, Idris Malagi, in his remarks, praised the choice of leadership of the council and said the APC would campaign on the administration’s record of transforming the Nigerian economy over the past three and a half years. He urged the newly appointed members to prioritise the collective good of the state and party unity The chairman of the APC North Central, Hon. Mu’azu Rijau, while congratulating the council leadership, stressed that the 2027 campaign council should not underestimate opponents, saying the party aimed to re-elect Governor Bago alongside its senators, House of Representatives members and state assembly members. Director-General of the campaign council, Ahmed Ibeto, accepted the assignment on behalf of members, pledging hard work, strategic coordination, grassroots engagement, unity, discipline and compliance with electoral guidelines. He said the council would establish operational frameworks across directorates, local governments, wards and units, and would value experience while welcoming new ideas. item.title: Temwa Chawinga becomes first African woman to finish in Ballon d’Or top 10
item.description: Malawian forward Temwa Chawinga has made history by becoming the first African woman to finish in the top 10 of the women’s Ballon d’Or. Chawinga’s achievement marks a significant milestone for African women’s football, placing the Malawi international among the world’s leading female players. Born on September 20, 1998, in Rumphi District, Malawi, Chawinga plays as a forward for Kansas City Current and the Malawi national team. She has enjoyed considerable success at club level, winning four Chinese Women’s Super League titles with Wuhan Jianghan University in 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023. She also won the NWSL x Liga MX Femenil Summer Cup in 2024 and the NWSL Shield in 2025 with Kansas City Current. Her individual honours include two consecutive NWSL Most Valuable Player awards in 2024 and 2025, as well as two NWSL Golden Boots in the same years. Chawinga also claimed the Chinese Women’s Super League Golden Boot in 2022 and 2023 before winning the International Federation of Football History and Statistics (IFFHS) World’s Best Top Goal Scorer award in 2023. She was joined in the Ballon d’Or top 10 by Haiti’s Melchie Dumornay, Norway’s Caroline Graham Hansen, Spain’s Patri Guijarro, Denmark’s Pernille Harder, Poland’s Ewa Pajor, Spain’s Clàudia Pina and Alexia Putellas, England’s Alessia Russo, and Jamaica’s Khadija Shaw. The list features players from Europe, Africa and the Caribbean, reflecting the growing global reach of women’s football. Chawinga’s historic finish represents a breakthrough for African representation in the prestigious individual award and further highlights her rise as one of the leading figures in the women’s game. item.title: Police confirm man, teenager swept away by flood in Aba
item.description: By Steve Oko Abia State Police Command has confirmed that a man who attempted to rescue a teenage girl from a water-filled ditch at Faulks Road, Aba, was swept away alongside the girl during Sunday’s downpour. The Police Public Relations Officer, Maureen Chinaka, disclosed this while responding to Vanguard inquiries, confirming that the incident occurred around the popular Ukwu Mango area of the commercial city. Chinaka said the tragedy happened near an ongoing construction site where an uncovered ditch had filled with rainwater. According to her, the teenage girl was passing through the area when she reportedly hit a stone and fell into the ditch. An adult who witnessed the incident reportedly plunged into the water in an attempt to rescue her, but both were swept away. “Unfortunately, we have not been able to see them. The police are aware, and the matter has been reported. Efforts are in place to see how they can be rescued,” Chinaka said. She confirmed that the two victims had yet to be found as search efforts continued. Asked whether the construction company responsible for the site would face possible charges over negligence, the police spokesperson said investigations were ongoing. The tragedy has raised concerns about the safety of construction sites during heavy rainfall, particularly where excavations and drainage channels are left uncovered and become submerged in floodwater. Aba’s flat terrain makes parts of the commercial city vulnerable to flooding during heavy downpours, increasing the risks posed by waterlogged roads, open drains and excavations. item.title: Impunity, justice system failure fuelling violence in North Central — Osinbajo
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa Former Vice President of Nigeria, Prof. Yemi Osinbajo, has attributed the widespread insecurity in North Central Nigeria and other parts of the country to failures in the justice system and inadequate punitive measures for crimes committed. Osinbajo stated this on Monday in Plateau State at a forum titled, “Countering Polarisation and Rebuilding Civic Cohesion in North Central Nigeria Beyond Tribe and Faith, Reclaiming Our Shared Stories,” organised by Justice Research Institute, JRI, in partnership with the National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies, NIPSS. The former Vice President said, “Impunity destroys the fabric of society. There must be clear and enforceable consequences for wrongdoing and offences committed against the state or individuals.” “If there are no consequences for actions taken under any guise, there will be no way to rebuild and reconcile. Peace cannot be built without justice.” “Those who have been displaced and whose communities or villages have been illegally occupied must be returned to their ancestral homes. item.title: El Niño: What it means and how Nigerians should prepare
item.description: By Sekinat Osundiji Nigeria may experience increased heat and changing rainfall patterns as a strengthening El Niño event raises concerns about its potential effects on agriculture, water supply, electricity generation and public health. The World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) said in September 2026 that El Niño was expected to strengthen into a very strong event and persist into early 2027. The Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) has also warned that the phenomenon could affect rainfall patterns, including the length of the rainy season and when it ends. But what is El Niño, how could it affect Nigeria, and what can the country do to prepare? What is El Niño? El Niño is a natural climate phenomenon that occurs when surface waters in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean become warmer than average. This warming affects atmospheric circulation, changing weather patterns around the world. Depending on the region, it can contribute to higher temperatures, reduced or excessive rainfall, and shifts in seasonal conditions. El Niño is part of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), a climate pattern that also includes La Niña, its cooler phase, and neutral conditions. According to the WMO, El Niño typically occurs every two to seven years and lasts between nine and 12 months. Although it develops thousands of kilometres from Nigeria, its influence on global atmospheric circulation can affect weather in West Africa. However, its effects vary by location and do not automatically mean drought or extreme heat everywhere. What does El Niño mean for Nigeria? NiMet’s August 2026 seasonal climate update identified the onset of a strong El Niño event and outlined possible implications for rainfall, agriculture, water resources and energy. For August to October 2026, the agency forecast normal to above-normal rainfall across much of northern Nigeria, while parts of the South-West and Cross River State were expected to experience normal to below-normal rainfall. Government agencies should also improve farmers’ access to timely weather information and agricultural advice. 3. Water supply and electricity generation Prolonged rainfall deficits can reduce river flows, reservoir levels and groundwater recharge, putting pressure on domestic water supplies and irrigation. Hydropower generation could also be affected if water inflows into dams decline. NiMet has identified reduced water availability and lower reservoir inflows as potential risks, although these do not confirm nationwide water shortages or electricity disruptions. Water authorities should monitor reservoirs and groundwater conditions, identify vulnerable communities and develop contingency plans. Residents can help by repairing leaking taps and avoiding unnecessary water waste. 4. Food prices and household expenses Adverse weather could reduce agricultural output, damage farms and disrupt transportation, placing pressure on food supplies and prices. However, El Niño alone does not mean food prices will rise nationwide. Harvests, storage, transport costs and wider market conditions will also influence prices. The government should monitor food supplies, support farmers in vulnerable areas and strengthen storage and distribution systems to reduce avoidable losses. How should Nigeria prepare? Preparation requires coordinated action by government agencies, state authorities, farmers, health workers, businesses and residents. NiMet should continue issuing updated, location-specific forecasts and ensure warnings reach rural communities and farmers, including those without reliable internet access. Health authorities should educate the public on heat-related illnesses and strengthen emergency responses, particularly for vulnerable populations. Agricultural ministries and extension officers should provide advice on planting dates, crop selection, irrigation and drainage based on current forecasts. Water agencies should monitor dams and reservoirs, reduce distribution losses and plan for communities that may face shortages. Authorities must also prepare for heavy rainfall and flooding rather than focus exclusively on drought. Government agencies, broadcasters and journalists should communicate climate information clearly, distinguish projections from confirmed events and update the public as conditions change. Does El Niño mean Nigeria is heading for disaster? Not necessarily. El Niño increases the likelihood of certain climate-related impacts but does not determine precisely what will happen in every state. The WMO has emphasised that even a very strong event does not produce equally severe effects everywhere. Local weather patterns and other climate drivers can alter its influence. Nigeria’s priority should be to identify areas most vulnerable to heat and rainfall changes and prepare accordingly. Following NiMet’s updates and taking practical precautions can help reduce risks to public health, agriculture, water resources and electricity generation. Ultimately, the challenge is not simply how strong El Niño becomes, but how effectively Nigeria prepares for its potential consequences. Climate resilience and environmental innovation will also be considered as an optional cross-cutting area. Participants are expected to develop working solutions, including AI-enabled applications, software prototypes, data-analysis tools, multilingual interfaces and other technically credible products. Idea-only submissions, presentations and mock-ups without functional solutions will not be accepted. The hackathon is open to Nigerians aged 18 and above, including developers, AI engineers, data scientists, cybersecurity professionals, researchers, civic-tech innovators, electoral experts, product designers and public policy practitioners. Applications may be submitted by individuals or teams of up to four members, with team-matching support available for individual applicants. Entries must be submitted in English, and projects that have already received grants, awards or recognition in previous competitions are ineligible. Speaking at the event, Dr Lawrence Bayode said the growing influence of AI on elections made it necessary for Nigeria to develop solutions that preserve electoral credibility. “The question before us is no longer whether AI has a role to play in an election, but how we can harness its potential without compromising the integrity, transparency and credibility of the electoral process,” he said. Four additional special innovation awards, each worth ₦500,000, will recognise outstanding work in research and policy innovation, electoral and civic inclusion, responsible AI and safety, and cybersecurity and resilience. Entries will be assessed based on technical functionality and innovation, relevance to electoral challenges, practical usefulness, cybersecurity, privacy, responsible AI, scalability, feasibility, demonstration and documentation. The organisers stressed that the initiative would not support partisan campaign technology, voter manipulation or interference with electoral administration. Participants are also prohibited from conducting unauthorised tests of live electoral systems or accessing institutional infrastructure. item.title: 2027: ADC dismisses APC’s 2m votes target for Tinubu in Jigawa‎
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa ‎The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has expressed confidence that its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, will win Jigawa State in the 2027 general elections, dismissing the All Progressives Congress (APC)’s target of delivering two million votes for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu as unrealistic. ‎The ADC candidate for Ringim/Taura Federal Constituency in Jigawa State, Hon. Shehu Sule Udi, stated this while reacting to the Jigawa APC’s declaration that it would deliver two million votes for Tinubu’s re-election. ‎Udi argued that the number of registered voters in Jigawa State made the APC’s target questionable, describing the declaration as political propaganda. ‎According to him, figures displayed by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) showed that Jigawa had 2,807,811 registered voters. ‎“This clearly shows that the party is just making propaganda,” he said. ‎“Look at how our presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, and other candidates in ADC are gaining support across Jigawa State every day. For somebody to tell you that they will deliver two million votes to Tinubu is ridiculous,” Udi stated. ‎He claimed that residents of the state were dissatisfied with the current administration because of the economic hardship facing Nigerians. ‎“People of Jigawa State are tired of this administration. They have suffered enough, and no reasonable person will vote for the APC in the coming election. ‎“Our presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, will win Jigawa State with massive votes and defeat President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. ‎Udi maintained that the ADC remained a credible alternative capable of addressing the economic challenges facing the country. ‎He expressed confidence that the growing support for the party across Jigawa State would translate into electoral victory in 2027. ‎The ADC candidate spoke while welcoming defectors from other political parties in Ringim and Taura Local Government Areas, describing their decision to join the party as a boost to its political strength ahead of the elections. item.title: Ebola patient arrives in Switzerland, as Nigeria sustains surveillance
item.description: By Sola Ogundipe Swiss authorities confirmed on Monday that Nigeria’s imported Ebola case and her spouse have arrived in Switzerland, where she is receiving treatment at Geneva University Hospitals while he remains in isolation at University Hospital Zurich. item.title: 2027: INEC puts preliminary voters’ register online, publishes final document Dec. 15
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has made the Preliminary Register of Voters for the 2027 General Election available on its online platform, following concerns raised by some stakeholders and in preparation for the certification and publication of the Final Register of Voters on December 15. The register can now be accessed at https://display.inecnigeria.org. It is the same list that was earlier displayed at Registration Areas nationwide. National Commissioner and Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee at INEC, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, said in a statement on Monday that the Commission “has taken note of the concerns expressed by Nigerians and other stakeholders regarding the desirability of making the Register accessible through its online platform in addition to the physical display already conducted.” “Accordingly, and in furtherance of its commitment to transparency, accessibility and public confidence in the electoral process, the Commission has decided to make available on its online platform https://display.inecnigeria.org the same Preliminary Register of Voters earlier displayed at the Registration Areas,” he said. Haruna recalled that the physical display was held in accordance with Section 19 of the Electoral Act, 2026, from 9th to 15th October, 2026. According to him, the exercise provided “registered voters the opportunity to inspect their particulars and submit claims and objections as prescribed by law.” He said the online publication does not replace the exercise already carried out. “This additional measure complements the physical display already undertaken and is intended to facilitate wider public access to the Register,” he said. The Commission said it is still processing the claims and objections that arose from the display. “Meanwhile, the Commission continues to process claims and objections arising from the exercise in accordance with the Electoral Act, 2026, preparatory to the certification and publication of the Final Register of Voters on 15th December 2026. “The Commission appreciates the continued interest and constructive engagement of Nigerians and stakeholders and reiterates its commitment to transparency, accountability and the faithful implementation of the Electoral Act, 2026 in delivering credible elections,” he said. item.title: Prof. Ochefu rejects appointment to NDC National Campaign Council
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi Professor of Economic History and Strategic Studies at Rev. Fr. Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi, Prof. Yakubu Ochefu, has rejected his purported appointment to the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) National Campaign Council, insisting that he is not a member of the party. Ochefu said he was neither consulted before his name was included in the list of members of the campaign council circulating on social media nor did he give his consent to the appointment. The university don, who is also the National Chairman of the Association of Nigerian Universities Alumni (ANUA) and President-General of Ochetoha K’Idoma, said his leadership positions required him to remain non-partisan, as the memberships of both organisations cut across political parties. In a statement he personally signed, Prof. Ochefu said, “My attention has been drawn to a list circulating on social media, titled ‘Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) National Campaign Council’, which names me as a member of its National Campaign Caucus. “I wish to inform the public that I am not a member of the NDC and have never been. “I was not consulted before my name was included, nor did I give consent. “I have written to the Chairman of the Council to decline the appointment and to request that my name be withdrawn and a revised list published. “As National Chairman of the Association of Nigerian Universities Alumni, ANUA, and President-General of Ochetoha K’Idoma, I lead organisations whose members cut across all political parties. These offices require me to remain non-partisan, and I intend to honour that obligation. “I thank all who reached out for clarification, and ask that you disregard the list insofar as it concerns me.” The post Prof. Ochefu rejects appointment to NDC National Campaign Council appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ADC to APC: Nigerians suffer, your youth leaders ride N1bn SUVs
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has slammed the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, over the reported distribution of seven luxury sports utility vehicles (SUVs) worth about N1 billion to its youth leaders, accusing the ruling party of prioritising political mobilisation over the hardship facing Nigerians. The opposition party said the reported distribution exposed the contradiction between the economic sacrifices Nigerians are being asked to make and the privileges enjoyed by the ruling party’s political operatives, with millions struggling to afford food, transportation and other necessities. In a statement on Monday, ADC National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, said the development raised questions about the APC’s priorities as it prepares for the 2027 general elections. “President Tinubu asks Nigerians to endure hardship while his party distributes luxury vehicles to its political operatives. Apparently, sacrifice is for ordinary Nigerians, while luxury is reserved for those working to keep the APC in power,” he said. Abdullahi said the ruling party had mobilised resources for its political machinery without offering a convincing answer to the rising cost of living. “The APC has found the resources to move its campaign officials around Nigeria. What it has failed to find is a convincing way to make life affordable for the Nigerians whose votes it now seeks,” he said. The ADC also questioned the rationale for providing the vehicles for grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 elections when youth unemployment and economic hardship remain major concerns. “Seven APC youth leaders can receive luxury vehicles, but millions of young Nigerians are still waiting for the jobs, opportunities and economic relief they were promised. Is this the APC’s idea of youth empowerment?” Abdullahi asked. The party demanded disclosure of the source of funding for the vehicles, including whether public resources were involved. “Nigerians deserve to know who paid for these vehicles. Until that question is answered, the ruling party cannot dismiss legitimate concerns about its priorities,” Abdullahi said. item.title: ADC fires back at APC over unpaid salary claims
item.description: dares ruling party to defend record By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has challenged the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to defend its record in government rather than make allegations against opposition parties, dismissing claims of unpaid salaries within the ADC as false and politically motivated. The party said the allegation was an attempt to divert attention from the economic hardship, rising cost of living, unemployment and insecurity confronting Nigerians, warning that the 2027 election debate should centre on the Tinubu administration’s performance. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC challenged the APC Presidential Campaign Council to produce evidence to substantiate its allegation, describing the claim as an attempt to distract Nigerians from the government’s record. “If the APC has any credible evidence to support its claims, it should produce it rather than continue to insult Nigerians with fabricated stories masquerading as press statements,” Abdullahi said. On the issues it believes should dominate public debate, the ADC said: “The real issue is the cost of living. The real issue is the absence of jobs and opportunities for our young people. The real issue is the insecurity that continues to threaten lives, livelihoods, and communities across the country.” The party also accused the APC of preparing for the 2027 elections by attacking opposition parties rather than presenting its achievements. “It is becoming increasingly clear that the APC has decided to run its 2027 campaign on allegations against the opposition rather than achievements of its own. That is what happens when a government has spent years making promises it cannot keep and excuses it cannot defend,” Abdullahi said. The ADC spokesman urged Minister of Information, Alake, and other APC officials to explain why Nigerians should support another term for the ruling party after three years of economic hardship and insecurity. “The APC may control the machinery of government, but it cannot control the lived experiences of Nigerians,” he said. Abdullahi said the ADC would remain focused on holding the Tinubu administration accountable, insisting that allegations against the opposition would not displace the economic concerns shaping public debate. “If the APC has a record to defend, let it defend it. If it has solutions, let it present them. But it should stop insulting the intelligence of Nigerians with these increasingly desperate distractions,” he added. The party maintained that the cost of living would remain central to its campaign, positioning the economic consequences of the Tinubu administration’s policies as a defining issue in the 2027 election. item.title: Mass killing threat: Enugu ex-lawmakers place N5m bounty on terrorist ringleaders
item.description: By Precious Enaike The Chairman of the forum of former members of Enugu State House of Assembly, Dr. Josef Onoh, announced Monday that they have placed a bounty of N5m on terrorists threatening mass killings in Enugu State after watching a viral video containing treasonable, cowardly and bloodthirsty threats of invasion against the peaceful domain of the state. These threats, Onoh said, issued by terrorists masquerading under whatever deceitful umbrella or criminal guise they claim, represent an intolerable assault on the collective security, sovereignty, and peace. Speaking on behalf of the Forum, in Abuja, Onoh categorically condemned the provocative rhetoric in the strongest possible terms and made it known clearly and unequivocally to the miscreants that Enugu State is not, and will never become, a playground for terrorists, bandits, or extremist agitators. According to him, stakeholders have built a heritage of peace, and no masked cowards chanting death threats will be allowed to disrupt the lives of the people. Onoh said the security of Enugu State remains paramount, and the forum will not fold its arms while fringe criminals attempt to intimidate our citizens or destabilize our homeland. “The forum stands resolutely behind the Enugu State Government and security agencies to crush any attempt at violating the peace of the state. To accelerate the wheels of justice and unmask every single criminal hiding under these guises, I have, on behalf of the forum of former members of Enugu State House of Assembly announced the strategic rewards of N5,000,000 (Five Million Naira) bounty for anyone who provides credible, actionable information to the Department of State Services (DSS), the Nigeria Police Force, or any other security agencies that leads directly to the arrest and prosecution of the main character chanting the death threats in the video, as well as any of his co-conspirators. “Furthermore, I would place a N50,000 (Fifty Thousand Naira) reward per name to any patriotic citizen who provides the full names and verified identities of each individual appearing in the video, along with details of their relatives, to the security agencies. I urge the DSS and all sister security apparatuses to launch an immediate, aggressive manhunt for the criminals. “To the good people of Enugu State, I urge them to remain calm, vigilant, and resilient and not be intimidated by the desperate rants of cowards while also reporting any suspicious movements or individuals to the nearest security agency immediately. Let me make it clear that Enugu State belongs to the peaceful and law-abiding individuals and forces of terror will always be defeated,” Onoh said. item.title: From Nigeria to Multiple Markets Across Borders: How SharpPunter Is Changing the Way Punters Analyse Sports

SharpPunter, a sports analysis platform built in Nigeria, was set up to give those punters a clearer look at what they are betting on before they place the slip. Six months after its launch in April 2026, it has users across West, East and Southern Africa, works with booking codes from 37 bookmakers and has just released V2, a rebuilt version of its app. Built in Nigeria, for the way Nigerians bet “I built SharpPunter because I was tired of seeing people stake their money on tips they had not checked by themselves, and I wanted something that would help punters truly understand which games were worth backing,” said Oluwatobi Abobade, who founded SharpPunter. “Over time, the way people use the product has shaped how we built V2. Users kept tagging our X bot with codes from friends, so checking a code is now one of the two things you see when you open the app. We also saw how closely people follow their own clubs and how often that turns their picks into emotional ones, so V2 lets you follow your club, get updates on its live matches and see the stats, alongside unbiased picks you can use.” Where slips go wrong, and what SharpPunter does about it The first problem is the tip itself, since most codes that circulate in group chats arrive with no rationale, and give punters no way to judge whether the picks are valid. Almost 100 per cent of the assets on land, in the swamp and shallow waters are owned by Nigerian indigenous companies. “Who is going to train the Nigerians? The new generation of Nigerians are coming behind to take over and operate those assets and work for these companies successfully,” he said. Training Centre Ogunsanya said Nigeria had sufficient human resources to develop its oil and gas industry, but needed to do more to attract graduates and provide them with practical skills. “The issue is not that we don’t have Nigerian young educated graduates that can come into the industry. The issue is how do we encourage these young educated Nigerian graduates to look into the oil and gas industry?” he asked. He said the industry required professionals with practical experience in drilling, pipeline installation, fabrication, welding and offshore operations, adding that training must prepare young Nigerians for the physical and technical demands of the sector. Ogunsanya disclosed that PETAN recruited nearly 100 engineers every two years through its internship programme, placing them in member companies for practical training. “After two years, PETAN members absorb over 60 per cent of these guys because that’s how good the training that we’re giving them is,” he said. He added that the association was working with the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board (NCDMB) on human capacity development initiatives. The chairman also disclosed plans to establish a training centre in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, with facilities, including drilling rigs, to train more Nigerian professionals locally. “If Shell will send 10 people to train, we can train 100 Nigerians if we bring the trainers into the country and we have the facilities,” he said. The PETAN boss warned that experienced Nigerian professionals were increasingly being recruited by countries in the Middle East, including Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, making local training investment more urgent. Drill-Or-Drop Policy Ogunsanya also backed the Federal Government’s drill-or-drop policy, which seeks to compel operators to develop their oil assets or risk losing them, describing it as critical to achieving Nigeria’s three-million-barrel-per-day production target. “The cheapest oil to produce in the world is already discovered, and we need to drill a few more wells to bring the oil,” he said. The PETAN chairman argued that developing existing discoveries could deliver additional production more quickly than relying exclusively on new exploration, which requires significant investment and carries geological risks. “We cannot have those assets sitting there that have potential to produce 10, 20, 50,000 barrels. Every drop of oil adds up to get to that three million barrels,” he said. According to him, enforcing the policy would also benefit indigenous service companies by increasing demand for drilling, equipment deployment and other technical services. He explained that service companies often have equipment and signed contracts but generate little revenue when operators fail to commence work. “If they say, ‘Ah, we don’t have work,’ you can have the contract in your hand, it’s signed. If they don’t call you, you don’t do any work,” he said. Ogunsanya added that increased activity would enable service companies to earn more revenue, purchase additional equipment and contribute to higher production. He also supported a review of aspects of the Nigerian Oil and Gas Industry Content Development Act, saying developments in the industry had created areas requiring attention. Gas Development Gaps The PETAN chairman also called for greater investment in gas production and distribution infrastructure, describing it as essential to expanding electricity generation and supporting industrial growth. He cited Nigeria’s estimated 210 trillion cubic feet of gas reserves and said the country had yet to maximise the resource’s potential across power generation, industry and domestic consumption. “This country needs a minimum of 100,000 megawatts of installed power capacity, and we will not have it unless we produce enough gas, unless we lay the pipelines where those gas turbines are going to be,” he said. Ogunsanya compared Nigeria’s installed electricity generation capacity of about 12,000 megawatts with the much higher capacities of South Africa and Egypt, arguing that increased gas utilisation was necessary to close the gap. He said the oil and gas industry remained central to Nigeria’s economic growth and urged operators, regulators and the government to address the constraints limiting investment and production.
